metadata.title: The fellows Skill
metadata.audience: Brutalist fellows already using Claude Code
metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/fellows/SKILL.md (SOURCE-SNAPSHOT SHA-256 afd14d36…; supervisor's episode.source_sha256 76651492…; re-verified run 616bfc2f — SKILL.md content unchanged, toolkit baseline updated). The reel explains that `fellows` is a FRAME around a fellow's own video report — Claude-branded bookends and Professor Bear's notes wrap the fellow's file, which plays untouched. Teaches: the required beat spine, THE REPORT IS THE CLOCK (inverts audio-first for one beat), FELLOW'S-WORK CARVE-OUT of REBUILD LAW, GATE N (Bear's notes are Bear's words), persistent Kokoro voice per fellow (with SOUND REPAIR carve-out for bad audio), and the STANDARD HAI outro deviation from the siblings' title-restate. No fellow's report is transcribed or shipped — this teardown is source-backed per SELF-DEMO LAW's feasibility fallback (running a real report would require a fellow's video, human approval of NOTES.md via GATE N, and the fellow's persistent voice choice). Kokoro am_onyx throughout — free, local. No captions. Outro is ClaudeTitleOutro (OUTRO-LOCK.md locks @NikBearBrown handle) because this is a claude-liam TEARDOWN; the fellows skill it explains uses a DIFFERENT outro (the HAI standard outro), and that deviation is the falsifiability beat itself. Portrait companion — native 9:16 layouts (not a center-crop of the landscape master). channel_title metadata deliberately omitted — its compile-overlay bleeds past portrait safe.b (documented in memory feedback_channel_title_portrait_bleed). Three SkillTeardown*916 wrappers are registered in this isolated toolkit's Root.tsx for this run; they share source with the landscape components and reflow via useVideoConfig().

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — anatomy of the fellows skill folder plus the fellow's episode folder.
beats.narration_text: First, the anatomy. On the toolkit side there is SKILL.md — the doctrine, one required beat spine, five laws of its own, and a persistent voice contract. On the fellow's side there is a per-episode folder: first-name last-initial, then a dated slug. Inside it: the transcript, the source video sitting in media, a NOTES markdown Bear must sign before Kokoro will speak them, and a build log. Small on disk. Human where it matters.

props.title: The fellows folders.
props.calloutText: NOTES.md is a human gate. The skill DRAFTS Professor Bear's notes from the transcript; Kokoro will not read them until Bear signs the exact wording.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — the required beat spine. Input: fellow's raw recording. Output: a wrapped reel + a signed NOTES.md.
beats.narration_text: The spine is fixed. Nine beats. The composer asks what the fellow has been working on. Two or three summary beats read from the transcript. Then the fellow's video plays as is — that is beat four. Two beats of Professor Bear's notes — feedback, then next steps. A Your Turn prompt, and the standard Humanitarians AI outro. Same shape every episode. Only the middle is the fellow's own material.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — THE REPORT IS THE CLOCK. Inverts the parent explainer's audio-first law for beat 4 only.
beats.narration_text: First design decision, and it is the sharpest. Every other Brutalist skill is audio-first — Kokoro generates the narration and the visuals conform to that clock. Fellows inverts that for exactly one beat. Beat four's clock is the report's own runtime. No trim, no speed change, no voiceover, no re-timing. The compiler transcodes container and resolution, and stops there. A trimmed cut is only legal when a human explicitly asks for it in the build log.

verdict pill 'inverts audio-first, for beat 4 only'

props.heading: The report is the clock.
props.body: Beat 4 is the ONE exception to audio-first. The report's own measured runtime drives that beat; its own audio stays on the timeline. Transcode container/resolution to reel spec (3840×2160 or 2160×3840, h264/AAC, contain/letterbox). NEVER trim, retime, speed up, or talk over it.
props.quote: THE REPORT IS THE CLOCK (the one exception to audio-first). Everywhere else narration MP3s are the master clock. The report beat's clock is the report's own measured runtime.
props.cite: fellows SKILL.md · THE REPORT IS THE CLOCK

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — FELLOW'S-WORK CARVE-OUT (of REBUILD LAW). Fellow's own frames play as themselves.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. Every claude explainer has a REBUILD law — figures and charts from a source are redrawn native, never screenshotted. Fellows carves out one exception. Frames pulled from the fellow's own report play as themselves — Ken Burns on a still, or the clip untouched. Their receipt is the point. Rebuilding it would falsify it. Everything else — context diagrams, notes cards, the credit card — stays under REBUILD law, in the humanitarians palette.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 2 lands
heading 'The carve-out.' fades in
body: fellow's frames = themselves; else = rebuild
quote block lands verbatim from SKILL.md
verdict pill 'the fellow's receipt is the point'

props.heading: The carve-out.
props.body: Fellow's OWN frames and clips play as themselves (Ken Burns for a still, the clip untouched for a moving frame). Everything ELSE — context diagrams, comparison charts, notes cards — is rebuilt native in the humanitarians palette. Sibling of cli-explainer's ACTUAL-CODE LAW.
props.quote: The fellow's artifact is the receipt; rebuilding it would falsify it. Everything that is NOT the fellow's own material is rebuilt native, REBUILD LAW unchanged.

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 — GATE N. Professor Bear's notes are Bear's words. Kokoro blocks pending or stale approvals.
beats.narration_text: Third decision, and it is where the skill earns its trust. Professor Bear's notes are Bear's words. The skill drafts them from the transcript, in plain register, as a starting point — but nothing goes to Kokoro until Bear has edited or signed NOTES markdown. The runtime hashes the notes and the exact spoken wording; a pending record, a stale hash, or a missing signature blocks Kokoro, Remotion, and any final. The dash-dash no-gate flag exists but it does not bypass this. Never have an AI sign a human's approval.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 3 lands
heading 'GATE N.' fades in
body: NOTES.md fingerprint + narration fingerprint
quote block lands verbatim from SKILL.md
verdict pill 'no bypass, no AI signing for a human'

props.heading: GATE N.
props.body: metadata.approvals.professor_notes binds two SHA-256 fingerprints: NOTES.md content + exact spoken narration. Pending, missing or stale records BLOCK Kokoro generation, Remotion rendering, and final export. --no-gate does not bypass. The code never signs for a human.
props.quote: The notes beats never go to audio until Bear has edited or signed NOTES.md. The runtime blocks pending or stale records; --no-gate is not a bypass. Never have an AI sign a human's approval record.

beats.role_note: Design decision 4 — PERSISTENT VOICE + SOUND REPAIR carve-out. Same fellow, same Kokoro voice across the series.
beats.narration_text: Fourth decision. Each fellow picks one Kokoro voice, once, and every episode in their series uses that voice. A name-based suggestion is a heuristic, never an identity claim. The fellow's explicit choice overrides it, and a later change is a documented re-voice for the whole series — never a silent per-episode swap. And the sound-repair carve-out: if the report's audio is bad — quiet, hummy, clipped — normalize it, denoise, high-pass. Timing stays. Voice stays. Every filter applied is logged in the build log.

props.heading: Persistent voice.
props.body: One Kokoro voice per fellow, across the whole series. The fellow's explicit choice overrides any name-based heuristic. SOUND REPAIR (carve-out inside the carve-out): loudness-normalize, denoise (afftdn / arnndn), high-pass — TIMING UNTOUCHED, log every filter in BUILD-LOG.md.
props.quote: Never pitch-shift, never time-stretch, never re-voice. Every filter applied is logged in BUILD-LOG.md.
props.verdictLabel: never pitch · never stretch · never re-voice
props.sparkLine: One voice. One fellow. One series.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — deliberate deviation from sibling skills. Fellows uses the standard HAI outro, NOT the title-restate ClaudeTitleOutro. Using the wrong outro is a defect, not a preference.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability, and this is where the fellows skill deliberately breaks from its siblings. Every other claude explainer closes on the title-restate outro — the one locked to at-NikBearBrown. Fellows does not. The last beat of a fellows reel is the standard Humanitarians AI outro, in the humanitarians palette. Same channel as the folder chip. If someone ships a fellows reel with the title-restate outro, that is a defect — not a style choice. The outro follows the channel, and the channel is HAI.

props.heading: A deliberate sibling break.
props.body: Every other claude-explainer uses ClaudeTitleOutro (locked @NikBearBrown, OUTRO-LOCK.md). Fellows uses the STANDARD HAI outro (OutroSeries / OutroCTA, humanitarians palette, content from AUTHOR.MD). Same channel as the folder chip. The wrong outro on a fellows reel is a defect.
props.quote: NOT the @NikBearBrown outro — fellows is a HAI channel reel; ClaudeTitleOutro and its lock (OUTRO-LOCK.md) do NOT apply here.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the skill in six lines.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Fellows is a frame around a fellow's own recording — nothing more, nothing less. The report is the clock, so the fellow's runtime rules beat four. The fellow's frames play as themselves. Professor Bear's notes require Bear's actual signature. The fellow picks a Kokoro voice once and keeps it across the whole series, and the audio can be repaired but never retimed. And the outro is the HAI outro — because fellows is a HAI reel. Skip any of these, and the frame breaks the very thing it exists to protect.

artifactLines: fellows wraps a fellow's own recording — the report itself plays untouched.
THE REPORT IS THE CLOCK: beat 4 inverts audio-first; source runtime rules.
FELLOW'S-WORK CARVE-OUT of REBUILD LAW: their frames play as themselves.
GATE N: NOTES.md is human-signed before Kokoro speaks it — no --no-gate bypass.
One Kokoro voice per fellow, across the whole series; SOUND REPAIR is legal, retiming is not.
The outro is the standard HAI outro — not ClaudeTitleOutro. The channel is @HumanitariansAI.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready prompt Liam reads aloud + discusses. Dry-run planning pass — no fellow's report needed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code: read the fellows skill, then plan — do not run — a dry-run fellows episode. Assume a hypothetical fellow with a two-minute report. Draft the composer ask, the two-beat summary from a fabricated transcript labeled clearly as a fixture, a NOTES markdown starter with feedback and next steps, a paste-ready Your Turn prompt, and the metadata approvals block for both voice and professor notes — with status pending. Read the plan and check three things. Does beat four's audio policy set preserve. Are both approvals authored as pending with fingerprints, not fake sign-offs. And does the outro name the standard HAI outro, never ClaudeTitleOutro.

props.segment: Plan a fellows reel without shipping it
props.command: Read skills/make/fellows/SKILL.md. Then plan (DO NOT RUN) a dry-run fellows episode for a hypothetical fellow with a 2-min report: (1) the ClaudeComposerAsk cold open; (2) two summary beats from a fabricated transcript LABELED as a fixture; (3) a starter NOTES.md with feedback + next steps; (4) a Your Turn prompt; (5) metadata.approvals for voice and professor_notes as PENDING records with real subject fingerprints. Do not run generate_audio_kokoro.py or compile.py.
output: check: does B04 declare kind: source_report + audio_policy: preserve?
check: are both approvals PENDING with real fingerprints (never fake sign-offs)?
check: does the outro name the standard HAI outro, not ClaudeTitleOutro?
